newsitem.title: USA: U.S. deplores arrest of leading dissident in Cuba.
newsitem.headline: U.S. deplores arrest of leading dissident in Cuba.

text.p: The United States on Tuesday deplored the arrest of a leading dissident in Cuba, charging that Cuban President Fidel Castro disregards human rights.

U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters that Hector Palacios Ruiz, leader of the opposition Democratic Solidarity Party in Cuba, had been arrested on Jan. 9 and charged with contempt of public authority.
Burns said the charges reportedly stemmed from statements Palacios made to European journalists about Cuba's intentions to abide by an international commitment to uphold democracy.
Castro, the only Communist head of state in the Americas, signed such a pledge at an Ibero-American summit held in Santiago, Chile, in November.

"The arrest of Mr. Palacios for expressing his views regarding the Cuban government is a clear indication that Castro continues to disregard the basic rights of the Cuban people to freedom of speech," Burns said.
"And we deplore the continuing repression and arrest of people who want to speak their mind in Cuba," he added.
The United States had denounced the detention of several Cuban dissidents last month at a time when Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy was visiting Havana.

Canada and the United States are close allies but have radically different policies toward Cuba. Washington has kept an embargo against the island for 35 years while Ottawa has become one of Havana's leading trade partners.
At the end of his trip to Havana, Axworthy signed a joint statement in which the Canadian government agreed to cooperate with Cuba on human rights issues.
Burns, who had questioned the political effect of the Canadian visit to Havana, said the United States hopes Canada will continue to look into Cuba's human rights situation.
"And frankly, as we said at the time, we're highly skeptical that the Cuban government, having made a public commitment, will meet that commitment," he added.

The United States chided Cuba last week in an official report, charging that its human rights record worsened last year after Castro's government cracked down on the dissident Concilio Cubano umbrella group.
Palacios is a member of Concilio Cubano, which Cuba views as a front financed by exiles in the United States.
